title: "Architecture"
toc-location: left
---

Quartorium is one small Node.js server and one web page. It has no external services: no
database server, no message queue, no login provider. It needs Git and Quarto on the same
machine, and a Git remote to push to.

::: {.column-page-right}
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph Browser
    A["Review page<br/>(React + TipTap)"]
    B["Admin page"]
  end
  subgraph Server["Quartorium server (Node.js)"]
    API["HTTP API<br/>api.js"]
    SVC["Review rounds<br/>rounds.js"]
    QMD["QMD pipeline<br/>qmd/*"]
    REV["Change tracking<br/>review.js"]
    RND["Renderer<br/>render.js"]
    GIT["Git plumbing<br/>git.js"]
    DB[("SQLite<br/>live state")]
  end
  P["Pandoc<br/>(bundled with Quarto)"]
  Q["Quarto"]
  R[("Git remote<br/>(any Git host)")]
  A <-->|JSON| API
  B <-->|JSON| API
  API --> SVC
  SVC --> QMD --> P
  SVC --> REV
  SVC --> RND --> Q
  SVC --> DB
  SVC --> GIT <-->|fetch / push| R
```
:::

## Design choices

**Git is the record, the database is the scratchpad.** Everything that matters long-term
(text, comments, decisions, who wrote what) is committed to Git. The database only holds what
is happening right now: drafts being typed, links, and which suggestions have been decided.
If you deleted the database, you would lose the open links and uncommitted drafts, but not
the paper or its history.

**Plain Git, no forge API.** The server keeps a bare clone of each repository and writes
commits with Git's plumbing commands (`hash-object`, `update-index`, `write-tree`,
`commit-tree`, `update-ref`, `merge-tree`), using a temporary index. It never needs a working
copy and never runs `checkout`. On main it only ever adds commits on top: a fast-forward to
the round, after merging what is new on main into the round first. Credentials are passed per command as an HTTP header and are never written
into the repository's configuration.

**Blocks, not characters.** Changes are tracked per paragraph (top-level block). Because
unchanged blocks keep their exact bytes ([How .qmd files are changed](qmd-files.qmd)),
comparing blocks by content is exact, and three-way merges are simple and predictable. The
word-level differences shown in the browser are computed only for display.

**Render once, cache by what matters.** Quarto renders the whole paper once. The cache key
covers everything that can change the outputs, which excludes the prose, so editing text
never triggers a re-render.

**Small dependency list.** Backend: Express, js-yaml, diff, nodemailer, and Node's built-in
SQLite driver (no native modules to compile). Frontend: React, TipTap, KaTeX, diff.

## Backend modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `server.js` | Creates the Express app, serves the built frontend, commits pending drafts and syncs with main on a timer, flushes on shutdown |
| `api.js` | HTTP routes (see [API](#api)) |
| `auth.js` | Admin password and signed session cookie; personal links need no login |
| `config.js` | Settings from environment variables |
| `db.js` | SQLite schema, small query helpers, JSON columns, migrations |
| `rounds.js` | The collaboration flow: projects, rounds, people, saving, changes, accepting, comments, commits, syncing with main, finishing, next round, history |
| `review.js` | Block-level change tracking: diff, three-way merge, apply a change, bring a copy up to date, merge two versions of the paper (`mergeQmd`) |
| `git.js` | Bare clone, fetch, push, plumbing commits, merges (with a custom merge for the paper), log, file reads |
| `render.js` | Quarto rendering, extracting each locked block's output, cross-reference numbers, asset cache |
| `references.js` | Reading the bibliography (`.bib`, `.bibtex`, CSL JSON via Pandoc) and labels in the paper |
| `mail.js` | Optional e-mails (invitations, new round, review finished) |
| `qmd/blocks.js` | Lossless splitting of a `.qmd` into blocks |
| `qmd/protect.js` | Wrapping Quarto-specific inline syntax before Pandoc |
| `qmd/pandoc.js` | Batch calls to Pandoc |
| `qmd/pm.js` | Pandoc document model ⇄ editor document |
| `qmd/document.js` | `parseQmd` / `serializeQmd`: the byte-preservation guarantee, locked-block enforcement, citation checks |
| `qmd/reflow.js` | Putting the author's line breaks back into an edited paragraph |
| `qmd/meta.js` | Reading and writing the comment block; migrating old files |

## Data model

```{mermaid}
erDiagram
  projects ||--o{ rounds : has
  rounds ||--o{ members : has
  rounds ||--o{ events : logs
  projects {
    text remote_url
    text base_branch
    text username
    text token
  }
  rounds {
    text doc_path
    text branch
    text status "open | finished"
    text base_text "the round's .qmd"
    int prose_version
    int committed_version
  }
  members {
    text name
    text role "lead | reviewer"
    text token "the personal link"
    text branch
    text copy_base "round text the copy started from"
    text copy_text "reviewer's draft"
    text resolved "decided suggestions"
    text orphans "outdated suggestions"
    text status "invited | working | done"
    text seen_prose "round text at last visit"
  }
  events {
    text type "edited | accepted | rejected | main | ..."
    text data
  }
```

- A **round** holds the current text of the paper under review (`base_text`, comments
  included). The lead's edits change it directly.
- A **reviewer** has a private copy: `copy_base` is the round text it started from, and
  `copy_text` is their version (null when they changed nothing). Their suggestions are the
  differences between the two.
- `resolved` remembers which suggestions the lead accepted or rejected, so they disappear
  from the list. `orphans` are suggestions that became *outdated* because the same
  paragraph changed in the round.
- **Events** record who changed which paragraphs, to explain *what changed since your last
  visit* across rounds.

On disk, the data folder (`QUARTORIUM_DATA`) contains `quartorium.sqlite`, `secret` (signs
the admin cookie), `repos/<id>.git` (bare clones) and `renders/<key>/` (rendered outputs and
their images).

## How a change flows

### Typing and saving

::: {.column-page-right}
```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser (reviewer)
  participant S as Server
  participant D as SQLite
  participant G as Git
  B->>S: PUT /api/r/:token/doc (editor document, rev)
  S->>S: serializeQmd: keep unchanged blocks, restore locked blocks by key, Pandoc for edited ones
  S->>D: copy_text = new text, rev + 1
  S-->>B: { rev }
  Note over B,S: others see the suggestion at their next poll (≤ 10 s)
  B->>S: POST /pause (page hidden) — or 10 min idle
  S->>G: commit "Anna's edits (in progress)" on Anna's branch
  S->>G: push (within ~30 s)
```
:::

The editor sends the whole document about a second after typing pauses. The `rev` number
protects against two open windows overwriting each other: a stale window is asked to reload.

### Seeing suggestions

For every reviewer, the server compares `copy_base` with `copy_text` block by block. Each run
of changed blocks is a suggestion, split into one suggestion per paragraph where paragraphs
correspond one to one. Suggestions from different people that touch the same paragraphs are
*competing*, and the lead picks one.

### Accepting

::: {.column-page-right}
```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant L as Browser (lead)
  participant S as Server
  participant G as Git
  L->>S: POST /changes/:id/accept
  S->>G: commit pending drafts first (reviewer's branch, round)
  S->>S: splice the reviewer's blocks into the round text
  S->>G: commit on the round branch, author = reviewer
  S->>S: mark as resolved, notify the reviewer, record event
  S-->>L: ok
```
:::

A suggestion can be applied only while the paragraphs it replaces are unchanged in the round.
Otherwise it's *outdated* and the lead copies from it by hand.

### Bringing a reviewer's copy up to date

When a reviewer opens their link and the round has changed, their copy is merged with the
round (a three-way merge on blocks: old base, their copy, new round):

- blocks only the round changed: the reviewer gets the new version;
- blocks only the reviewer changed: their edits are kept;
- blocks both changed: the round's version wins and the reviewer's version is kept as an
  *outdated* suggestion, so nothing is lost and nothing is silently overwritten;
- suggestions the lead rejected are dropped from the copy.

This happens only on page load, never while someone is typing, so text never shifts under
the cursor. The next commit on the reviewer's branch records the round commit as a second
parent.

### Syncing with main

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant M as main (remote)
  participant S as Server
  participant R as round branch
  Note over S: every minute, when a lead opens the paper,<br/>or "Sync with main now"
  S->>M: fetch
  alt main has commits the round doesn't
    S->>R: commit pending edits
    S->>R: merge main: other files by Git,<br/>the paper paragraph by paragraph (mergeQmd)
    Note over S,R: same paragraph changed on both sides:<br/>main's version kept, the round's attached as a comment
  end
  opt main is kept up to date
    S->>M: push the round's head to main (fast-forward)
  end
```

`mergeQmd` splits the base, round and main versions of the paper into blocks, takes the
comment block out of all three, and runs the same three-way block merge used for reviewers'
copies. Blocks changed on one side are taken from that side, and blocks added at the same
place on both sides are both kept. When both sides changed the same block, main wins and the
round's version is returned so that it can be attached as a comment. Comment threads are
merged by id: replies and agreements from both sides are combined, and a thread removed on
one side stays removed. The merge commit is then written with Git's plumbing like any other.

If pushing to main fails because main moved in the meantime, the next sync catches up. If it
fails for another reason (a protected branch), automatic updates are switched off for the
repository and the lead sees why.

## Rendering

::: {.column-page-right}
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["git archive<br/>of the round"] --> B["write the .qmd with each locked block<br/>wrapped in ::: {#qtm-N}"]
  B --> C["quarto render --to html"]
  C --> D["cut out each block's HTML<br/>copy images to the cache"]
  C --> E["read figure / table / equation /<br/>section numbers"]
  D --> F[("renders/&lt;key&gt;/")]
  E --> F
```
:::

- The cache key is a hash of the repository tree without the paper, the paper's path, and
  the source of every locked block. Prose edits don't change it; editing a code chunk on main
  and a push to main that changes a code chunk do.
- Renders run one at a time, in the background. The page shows the source of locked blocks
  until the output is ready.
- Code chunks are shown as their output (the code is available under *Show source*).
- Cross-reference numbers (`@fig-mpg` → "Figure 1") come from the rendered HTML, so they
  match the paper exactly.

## Inline track changes in the browser

The editor shows three kinds of marks, all computed from block keys plus a word diff
(`diffWordsWithSpace`):

| Who sees it | What | Based on |
|---|---|---|
| Reviewer | their own edits (green insertions, struck deletions) | their copy vs. the round text it started from |
| Everyone | what changed since their last visit | the round text now vs. the round text at their last visit |
| Lead, in the review queue | a preview of the suggestion in place | the suggestion's old vs. new blocks |

The marks are decorations: they're drawn over the text and never become part of the
document, so they can't leak into the `.qmd`.

## API {#api}

All routes are under `/api`. Personal-link routes are under `/api/r/:token`. The token is the
only credential, and lead-only actions check the role.

| Method | Route | Purpose | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/login`, `/admin/logout` | admin session | admin |
| GET | `/admin/session` | is this browser logged in as admin? | anyone |
| GET / POST | `/projects` | list / connect repositories | admin |
| DELETE | `/projects/:id` | disconnect a repository | admin |
| GET | `/projects/:id/files` | `.qmd` files on the base branch | admin |
| POST | `/projects/:id/rounds` | start a round (returns the lead's link) | admin |
| GET | `/rounds/:id` | round details | admin |
| GET | `/r/:token` | open the paper: document, comments, suggestions, people, render, references, since last visit | link |
| GET | `/r/:token/activity` | polling: suggestions, comments, people, render status | link |
| PUT | `/r/:token/doc` | save the draft | link |
| POST | `/r/:token/comments` | new comment or reference request | link |
| POST | `/r/:token/comments/:cid/replies` · `/resolve` · `/agree` | reply, resolve, agree | link |
| POST | `/r/:token/changes/:id/accept` · `/reject` | decide a suggestion (reviewers may withdraw their own) | lead |
| POST | `/r/:token/changes/accept-all` | accept all that don't conflict (optionally from one person) | lead |
| POST / DELETE | `/r/:token/people`, `/people/:id` | invite / remove a person | lead |
| POST | `/r/:token/people/:id/invite` | send or prepare the invitation e-mail | lead |
| POST | `/r/:token/pause` | the page was left: commit the draft | link |
| POST | `/r/:token/finish` | finish my review (with a note) | reviewer |
| POST | `/r/:token/round/finish` · `/reopen` · `/merge` · `/next` | round lifecycle | lead |
| GET | `/r/:token/rounds` | earlier rounds | lead |
| POST | `/r/:token/sync` | sync with main now: bring in main, and update main if it's kept up to date | lead |
| POST | `/r/:token/round/keep-main` | keep main up to date automatically, on or off | lead |
| POST | `/r/:token/render` | render again | link |
| GET | `/r/:token/history`, `/history/:hash` | history, and one entry's changes | link |
| GET | `/render/:key/*path` | rendered images and other assets (immutable) | anyone with the key |

## Tests

`npm test` runs the backend tests with Node's built-in test runner:

- `qmd.test.js`: lossless splitting, unchanged round trips, one-line diffs, protected
  syntax, locked-block enforcement, citations, comments, legacy migration;
- `review.test.js`: diff, merge, competing and outdated suggestions;
- `git.test.js`: plumbing commits, merges and pushes against a local bare remote;
- `render.test.js`: a real Quarto render with a figure, a table and cross-references;
- `main-sync.test.js`: the lead working in RStudio during a round: code, figures and text
  pushed to main come into the round, accepted text reaches main, the same paragraph changed
  on both sides, a protected main;
- `flow.test.js`: a complete review: invite, edit, comment, cite, accept, decline, finish
  review, leave the page, history, finish round, merge into main, next round with the same
  links, e-mails.
